name: ATR expansion momentum breakout (5m)
rationale: A rising ATR on 5m signals a volatility expansion; pairing it with a positive short return says the expansion is directional, not two-sided chop. Entering as ATR expands with momentum catches the breakout bar before the move fully unfolds. The other side is the mean-reversion maker who fades every spike and is wrong when the spike is a real breakout. Edge persists because volatility expansions are autocorrelated and the initial thrust tends to continue for several bars. Distinct from the bandwidth-squeeze spec: this triggers on ATR level rising (not prior compression) and requires a return leg. Disconfirmer: exits when the short return flips negative, or the stop fires.
